fi-poecilia-reticulata.title: Guppy
fi-poecilia-reticulata.summary: The guppy, Poecilia reticulata, is a livebearer native to northeastern South America and the southern Caribbean, including Venezuela and Trinidad. One of the most popular aquarium fish in the world,…
rows: Wild fish are primarily insectivorous, but today's tank-bred fish are far-removed from their ancestors and will accept most foods offered.
Native to northeastern South America and the southern Caribbean with its original range considered to cover Venezuela , Guyana , Suriname , French Guiana plus the islands of…
notes: Unfussy, though a planted tank with floating vegetation is appreciated.

fi-carassius-auratus.title: Goldfish
fi-carassius-auratus.summary: A cold-tolerant carp relative kept as single-tail commons/comets and many fancy double-tail varieties. Needs cool, well-filtered water and more space than most tropical community fish.
rows: Commons/comets large; fancy forms typically several inches body length
About 20 gal for the first fancy goldfish, plus ~10 gal per additional fish; commons/comets need still more room. Prefer wide tanks with lots of surface area
Peaceful with other goldfish; not ideal with most tropical community fish because of temperature and waste load
Fine singly or in groups of goldfish; avoid nippy or hot-water tankmates
Omnivore. Quality pellets plus frozen foods and greens; avoid chronic overfeeding (bloat risk)
About 50–70°F (10–21°C) for fancy goldfish; room temperature is often fine — they are cold-water fish
Easy physically, but demanding on space and filtration because of heavy waste
Domesticated from wild Carassius stocks in East Asia; now a worldwide ornamental
notes: Strong filtration and regular water changes matter more than a heater in most homes.
Feeder comets are the same species — treat them as real pets with proper tank size if you keep them long-term.

fi-pimephales-promelas.title: Rosy Red Minnow (Fathead)
fi-pimephales-promelas.summary: A hardy North American minnow sold as “rosy reds,” often as feeders but also kept as cold-tolerant pets. Peaceful schooling fish for cool aquariums or ponds.
rows: Usually 2–3 in in aquariums; FishBase max about about 7 cm
About 20 gal or larger for a small school
Omnivore. Flake, pellets, and frozen foods; also used as feeder fish
Cool to temperate — about 50–78°F (10–26°C); happier cooler than most tropicals
notes: Shop “feeder rosy red” and pet-quality listings are the same species.

in-ghost-shrimp.title: Ghost Shrimp
in-ghost-shrimp.sci: Palaemonetes / related glass shrimp (trade “ghost shrimp”; catalog Natantia gen. sp.)
in-ghost-shrimp.summary: Small, mostly clear freshwater shrimp sold as cleaners or feeders. Hardy omnivores that scavenge leftover food; exact species in the trade is often mixed.
rows: 5–10 gal or larger; fine in community tanks without shrimp predators
Peaceful; may be eaten by larger fish
Omnivore / scavenger — biofilm, leftover foods, blanched veg, shrimp pellets
Various; many US trade ghost shrimp are Palaemonetes species
notes: Catalog lists Natantia gen. sp. — trade ghost shrimp are not a single verified species.
warn: May be preyed on by larger fish, crabs, or aggressively hungry tankmates.
